# epsilonInsensitiveGradient

> Compute the [epsilon insensitive loss gradient][epsilon-insensitive-loss-gradient] with respect to a model parameter for a single-precision floating-point number.

<section class="intro">

The [epsilon insensitive loss gradient][epsilon-insensitive-loss-gradient] is defined as

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:epsilon_insensitive_loss_gradient" align="center" raw="\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial w} =\begin{cases}-x & \text{if } y - p > \epsilon, \\x & \text{if } p - y > \epsilon, \\0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}" alt="Equation for the epsilon insensitive loss gradient."> -->

```math
\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial w} =\begin{cases}-x & \text{if } y - p > \epsilon, \\x & \text{if } p - y > \epsilon, \\0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
```

<!-- </equation> -->

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

<!-- eslint-disable id-length -->

```javascript
var epsilonInsensitiveGradient = require( '@stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/epsilon-insensitive-gradient' );
```

#### epsilonInsensitiveGradient( x, e, y, p )

Computes the [epsilon insensitive loss gradient][epsilon-insensitive-loss-gradient] with respect to a model parameter for a single-precision floating-point number.

<!-- eslint-disable id-length -->

```javascript
var v = epsilonInsensitiveGradient( 3.0, 5.0, 10.2, 0.782 );
// returns -3.0

v = epsilonInsensitiveGradient( -1.3, 1.0, 23.2, -0.999 );
// returns ~1.3
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **x**: input value.
-   **e**: insensitivity parameter.
-   **y**: true target value.
-   **p**: predicted value.

If any argument is `NaN`, the function returns `NaN`.

<!-- eslint-disable id-length -->

```javascript
var v = epsilonInsensitiveGradient( NaN, 1.0, 1.0, 0.782 );
// returns NaN

v = epsilonInsensitiveGradient( 1.0, 1.0, NaN, 0.782 );
// returns NaN

v = epsilonInsensitiveGradient( NaN, NaN, 1.0, 0.782 );
// returns NaN

v = epsilonInsensitiveGradient( NaN, NaN, NaN, NaN );
// returns NaN
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint-disable id-length -->

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/uniform' );
var logEachMap = require( '@stdlib/console/log-each-map' );
var epsilonInsensitiveGradient = require( '@stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/epsilon-insensitive-gradient' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float32'
};
var x = uniform( 100, -100.0, 100.0, opts );
var e = uniform( 100, 0.0, 5.0, opts );
var y = uniform( 100, -100.0, 100.0, opts );
var p = uniform( 100, -5.0, 5.0, opts );

logEachMap( 'epsilonInsensitiveGradient(%0.4f, %0.4f, %0.4f, %0.4f) = %0.4f', x, e, y, p, epsilonInsensitiveGradient );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/epsilon_insensitive_gradient.h"
```

#### stdlib_base_float32_epsilon_insensitive_gradient( x, e, y, p )

Computes the [epsilon insensitive loss gradient][epsilon-insensitive-loss-gradient] with respect to a model parameter for a single-precision floating-point number.

```c
float out = stdlib_base_float32_epsilon_insensitive_gradient( 3.0f, 5.0f, 10.2f, 0.782f );
// returns -3.0f
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **x**: `[in] float` input value.
-   **e**: `[in] float` insensitivity parameter.
-   **y**: `[in] float` true target value.
-   **p**: `[in] float` predicted value.

```c
float stdlib_base_float32_epsilon_insensitive_gradient( const float x, const float e, const float y, const float p );
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- C API usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/ml/base/loss/float32/epsilon_insensitive_gradient.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main( void ) {
    const float x[] = { -10.0f, -9.56f, -8.67f, -7.78f, -6.89f, 6.89f, 7.78f, 8.67f, 9.56f, 10.0f };
    const float e[] = { 0.0f, 1.0f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 5.0f, 6.0f, 7.0f, 8.0f, 9.0f };
    const float y[] = { -9.9f, -7.7f, -5.5f, -3.3f, -1.1f, 1.1f, 3.3f, 5.5f, 7.7f, 9.9f };
    const float p[] = { -5.0f, -3.89f, -2.78f, -1.67f, -0.56f, 0.56f, 1.67f, 2.78f, 3.89f, 5.0f };

    float v;
    int i;
    for ( i = 0; i < 10; i++ ) {
        v = stdlib_base_float32_epsilon_insensitive_gradient( x[ i ], e[ i ], y[ i ], p[ i ] );
        printf( "epsilonInsensitiveGradient(%f, %f, %f, %f) = %f\n", x[ i ], e[ i ], y[ i ], p[ i ], v );
    }
}
```

</section>
